Moraga.headline: Moraga: Spotty showers tonight, then a brief break before the next storm
Moraga.text: Moraga’s next 24 hours look unsettled but not like a washout: a weakening front is edging into the Bay Area this evening, and showers may reach the inland valleys, though guidance differs on how much rain survives the trip south. A few more showers are possible Sunday afternoon or evening, with lows near 40°F and highs in the lower-to-middle 50s. Monday should turn mainly dry. A stronger Tuesday–Wednesday system could bring a more meaningful round of rain and gusty winds, with Bay Area totals generally 0.5–1.5 inches and higher amounts toward the coastal ranges.

Lafayette.headline: Lafayette: The weekend front fades, but a stronger system is lining up
Lafayette.text: Lafayette may catch a few showers this evening as a weakening front slides across the Bay Area, but the rain band is expected to lose organization as it pushes south and inland. Sunday brings another spotty shower chance, mainly afternoon or evening, while cool nights and highs in the low-to-mid 50s keep the weekend feeling wintry. Monday looks mainly dry. Attention then shifts to Tuesday and Wednesday, when a stronger system could bring widespread rain and 20–30 mph gusts across much of the region, with locally stronger winds through exposed gaps.

Danville.headline: Danville: A few showers may slip through before Monday’s dry pause
Danville.text: Danville sits near the southern edge of the weakening weekend front, so any rain reaching the valley this evening may be scattered rather than steady. A few more showers could pop up Sunday afternoon or evening, with a cool night near 40°F and daytime temperatures mostly in the 50s. Monday is expected to be mainly dry. The next system arrives Tuesday into Wednesday, bringing a better chance of widespread rain and breezier conditions; keep drainage clear as the pattern turns wetter again.

Greenbrook.headline: Danville: Greenbrook sees a spotty shower risk, then a midweek turn
Greenbrook.text: Danville’s Greenbrook area shares the valley’s unsettled setup: the weakening front may deliver a few scattered showers this evening, but guidance differs on how far south the rain holds together. Sunday could bring another brief shower, mainly later in the day, with cool temperatures continuing. Monday looks like a mostly dry pause. A stronger Tuesday–Wednesday system is the next concern, with broader rain and gusty winds possible across the East Bay; localized runoff may become an issue where drains are blocked.

Marin City.headline: Marin City: Showers ease, but high Bay water becomes the bigger concern
Marin City.text: Marin City may see passing showers this evening and again Sunday, although the weekend front is weakening as it moves through. The more consequential local issue is rising Bay water: a Coastal Flood Advisory remains in place through 6 a.m. Monday, then a Coastal Flood Warning is scheduled from 6 a.m. Monday through 4 p.m. Thursday for San Francisco and San Pablo Bay shorelines. Tuesday and Wednesday’s stronger storm could add rain and runoff to already elevated water levels. Keep watch on low-lying waterfront access and heed any closures.

Sausalito.headline: Sausalito: King tides and a midweek storm put the waterfront on alert
Sausalito.text: Sausalito’s immediate weather stays showery rather than stormy, with a weakening front moving through this evening and a few more showers possible Sunday. The bigger concern is water levels: the Bay shoreline Coastal Flood Advisory runs through 6 a.m. Monday, then a Coastal Flood Warning takes over through 4 p.m. Thursday. At the San Francisco gauge, high tides are forecast near 8.4 feet Tuesday and 8.6 feet Wednesday, including a modeled surge contribution; timing and levels vary around the Bay. A stronger Tuesday–Wednesday storm may compound flooding, so watch marina approaches and low-lying waterfront roads.

Brentwood.headline: Brentwood: A few showers may clip the Delta before a dry Monday
Brentwood.text: Brentwood’s evening forecast is mostly cloudy, with the weakening front bringing only a spotty shower risk as it moves across Northern California. Sunday may bring another brief shower chance, but the weekend system is expected to be minor and much of the Delta should avoid meaningful rainfall. Monday turns mainly dry, with cool conditions holding. The next system arrives Tuesday into Wednesday; current NWS guidance points to a wetter, breezier stretch for the Bay Area, though the heaviest totals should favor the North Bay and coastal ranges rather than the inland Delta.

East Sacramento.headline: East Sacramento: Light rain returns, then a dry Monday break
East Sacramento.text: East Sacramento may see light rain spread into the city tonight, with another chance of showers Sunday afternoon; NWS Sacramento keeps most Valley weekend totals around 0.10 inch or less. Monday looks dry and cool, offering a short break. Rain chances rise again Tuesday into Wednesday, but the latest NWS discussion expects a weaker system than last week, with lower totals and lighter winds. The main travel impacts should favor the Sierra, where snow levels rise from roughly 4,000–5,000 feet Tuesday to above 7,000 feet by Thanksgiving.
